text:
maya: Heads up — us-west2 edge stack is showing a sudden drop in healthy targets for model-serving group A. ALB reports failing health checks, 0/6 targets registered.
liam: any deploys or infra changes in the last hour?
maya: none from infra deploys, but buildbot pushed a canary earlier. health check is TCP:443 / status 200 check at /healthz
chandra: can you paste the ALB target health output?
maya: ops-bot:alb-check --target-group tg-0a1b2c3d
ops-bot: ALB TG tg-0a1b2c3d - 6 targets: 0 healthy, 6 unhealthy. reason: Timeout. last_status: 504
ben: timeout looks like traffic from ALB not reaching pod or SG blocking return path
liam: maya can you curl LB IP from within the subnet? also describe SG rules on the instance ENIs
maya: running: curl -v http://10.12.45.233:443/healthz
maya: * connect to 10.12.45.233 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
chandra: show sg for the ENI: aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0abc1234 --query 'Groups[*].GroupId'
maya: returned sg-0d1e2f3a (svc-instances)
liam: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0d1e2f3a --query 'IpPermissions'
liam: output: [ { FromPort: 443, ToPort: 443, IpRanges: [ { CidrIp: "10.0.0.0/16" } ] } ]
maya: wait that CIDR is VPC internal only, ALB is in public subnets with ephemeral IPs — health checks come from ALB subnets, not 10.0.0.0/16
ben: oh wow someone tightened SG to VPC CIDR only (probably to restrict access), so ALB health checks are blocked
chandra: but why would outbound from pod to ALB fail? health check is inbound to pods on 443 from ALB; return traffic allowed only if ephemeral ports are permitted on SG
liam: check ALB SG too: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0f1e2d3c
maya: ALB SG shows 0.0.0.0/0 egress allowed. inbound allows 0.0.0.0/0:443
ben: root cause: instance SG only allowed 10.0.0.0/16:443, and ALB source IPs are in ALB subnet CIDRs (e.g., 3.121.45.0/28) — they are outside that range
maya: quick mitigation: add ALB subnets CIDRs to instance SG or set IpRange to the ALB SG as source (recommended)
chandra: ops-bot:authorize-sg-ingress --group-id sg-0d1e2f3a --protocol tcp --port 443 --source-group sg-0f1e2d3c
ops-bot: Success - ingress rule added
maya: re-checking targets...
ops-bot: ALB TG tg-0a1b2c3d - 6 targets: 6 healthy
liam: nice. who made the SG change? need audit and avoid schema where people replace allowed sources with VPC/CIDR
ben: I saw a PR in infra-configs #422 with revert of 0.0.0.0 -> 10.0.0.0/16, staged around 1745230500
chandra: okay we'll add a pre-merge check: disallow replacing ALB/source-group references with VPC CIDR if TG exists
maya: also add a doc note: ALB -> targets require instance SG to allow ALB SG or ALB subnet CIDRs; don't rely on VPC CIDR
liam: follow-up: check NACLs on the subnet? if NACL was deny high-ports it would break return path
maya: subnet NACLs are default allow. So this was purely SG config drift
ben: logging: created ticket INFRA-912 and tagged people who merged the change
maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
chandra: we should also add an alert rule: if ALB registered targets drops by >50% for 3m, page oncall
liam: agreed - i'll open a PR for alerting and the sg-checker rule
maya: closing loop: health stabilized, rolling back the overly strict SG change and adding automation
ben: summary for postmortem: misconfigured instance SG restricting source to VPC CIDR blocked ALB health checks -> 0/6 targets -> traffic degraded. Mitigations: revert rule, add pre-merge SG validation, alerting for dropped targets.
maya: thanks everyone, marking resolved.
